entries.text: An agent's own worker-to-leader comment no longer starts the same agent again in another role.
Only owners can change workspace, squad and agent instructions, with compare-and-swap protection against overwriting edits.
Release builds carry one ICT build stamp, and updates keep the correct version order.
Scheduled autopilots and recurring wakeups pause for 60 minutes after a provider server failure and resume only once it answers 401.
Rate-limited PR wakeups now recover atomically and can no longer be revived by switching them off and on.
Issue owners are now woken by default when a linked PR merges or its CI fails.
multica update and the daemon now update Linux and macOS builds from successful fork main CI artifacts.
Owners can pause a daemon for maintenance with multica daemon maintenance and set agent environment values conditionally.
Hermes agents can opt in to an external memory backend, per agent.
Hermes and Codex runs on GPT-6 Sol and Luna now report their cost.
The CLI can send an expected digest so governed workspace and squad fields change only if nobody edited them first.
Long-running Codex issue threads now start fresh instead of resuming with a broken tool setup.
Codex runs that wrongly claim they have no CLI access are now retried, or failed fast.
Codex agents on GPT-5.6 and GPT-6 models keep their shell tool.
Workspaces can set how long export audit manifests are kept (90 days by default).
Codex runs that died at start with a SQLite init error now retry once.
New multica provenance export command writes an audited, redacted, read-only export of issue and thread records.
multica squad update can read instructions from a file or stdin without shell escaping.
Workspaces can opt in to server-side checks that agent writes cite the required source link of an issue, including raw CLI and API calls.
The provider hold now also blocks task retries and claims, not only new triggers.
Agent runs now start with a checkpoint briefing that tracks which comment threads changed since the last run.
Sub-issues now close themselves instead of parking at in review, so parent stages no longer stall.
Deploys now switch between blue and green app slots with one atomic cutover.
When a provider is on hold, dispatching to it now fails with a clear policy message instead of a 503 error.
Status questions get an instant answer without a model call, in the issue comment box and in three CLI reads.
Assigning an issue no longer starts a duplicate run when the agent already has one pending.
Qualified main builds now deploy to C00 automatically, with a bounded rollback if the deploy fails.
Autopilot create-issue no longer fails when a duplicate pending task already exists.
Completing a stage now wakes the parent issue once instead of twice.
"Show N more replies" now expands a comment thread; the button no longer vanishes mid-click.
Show more / Show less on issue descriptions is now a visible button with a hover state and a smooth expand animation.
Find (Ctrl/Cmd+F) and notification links now open folded content before jumping to it.
Quoting "Closes X" in code no longer closes an issue, and an issue with open sub-issues no longer auto-closes.
Fold all no longer re-expands threads that have an active draft or run.
Comment threads can be folded, including Fold all, and replies and agent runs now sit in one chronological order.
multica issue comment resolve --known-as-of refuses to resolve a thread that changed after you last read it.
Two simultaneous reruns of the same task no longer cancel each other's run.
Double-clicking or retrying Rerun no longer starts a second run.
Long issue descriptions now collapse behind a Show more / Show less control.
Agents can no longer silently change agent, squad, workspace or project instructions through the generic update API.
One GitHub App can now serve several GitHub organizations in the same workspace.
multica issue update --expected-revision rejects stale writes; resolving a comment and recovery dispatch no longer race.
Squad leaders no longer risk publishing the same candidate twice when a merge event and a human reply arrive together.
Squad leaders must check the issue before deciding to do nothing, so a human comment no longer leaves a silent, empty run.
New projects get the default workflow at once, and a project change made together with a status change applies in order.
Issue statuses can follow a customizable workflow; multica issue transitions lists the allowed next statuses.
Issue pages now show a Graph in the sidebar with the parent and sub-issue tree.
